places.blurb: Planned park on the Frio River country near Garner State Park. Not open yet; TPWD is still planning it.
places.status_note: Not yet open. The TPWD page says: This park is not yet open. It is in the planning stage of development. Entrance page says: Site not open: Contact the Park.
places.notes: Address 2503 CR 349, Concan, TX 78838 (TPWD page). The TPWD page does not print a county or acreage. County Uvalde and the 1,720-acre figure come from August 2025 news coverage (HPPR, KSAT, Houston Chronicle list), not from an official or Wikipedia page, so per the brief acres is null. The Wikipedia URL guess for this park returned 404. Camping kinds not stated (not open). reservations_url left null: the TPWD page links only the general reservations pages. dark_sky null: darksky.org places page returned 403, and TPWD's dark-sky list does not name this unit. Ten candidates for my name, for the orchestrator: Lodestar, Wayfarer, Starlamp, Kestrelwing, Hollowstone, Brightwater, Tinderbox, Cartograph, Nightjar, Ledgerfield. Chosen: Nightjar.

places.name: Cleburne State Park
places.coord_point: park coordinates as printed on the TPWD page (point type not stated)
places.blurb: Cedar Lake and wooded campsites about 30 minutes southwest of Fort Worth, with cabins and a group camp.
places.status_note: TPWD says We often reach capacity and recommends reservations. No closure found.
places.notes: TPWD printed 32.252365, -97.549617. Wikipedia infobox gives 32.25250, -97.54972 (no source named), about 17 m apart, so the two sources agree. TPWD address 5800 Park Road 21, Cleburne, TX 76033. Campsites have water and electricity, some with sewer. Tent camping not stated on the page, so tent is left out. The 116 acre figure is Cedar Lake, not the park. Acreage 528 is the Wikipedia total park area.

Lake Casa Blanca International State Park is left out of nearby because the TPWD page gives no distance and I did not measure one.

places.blurb: Over 5,000 acres of Hill Country brush and trails, with walk-in camps, equestrian sites and a group camp with stalls.
places.status_note: The TPWD page says trails and backcountry campsites may close due to wet conditions or poor weather. It also shows This park has active alerts, whose text I did not read.
places.notes: TPWD printed 29.628034, -99.181086. Wikipedia infobox gives 29.62778, -99.18056 (no source named), about 60 m apart. Address 10600 Bandera Creek Road, Bandera, TX 78003. TPWD says over 5,000 acres; Wikipedia gives 5,369 acres, which is used. Wikipedia places the preserve on the Bandera and Medina county line, so county is given as Bandera with that caveat. Wikipedia says camping is limited to nine walk-in campsites and three hike-in areas plus five equestrian sites, and the group lodge has electricity. Phone (512) 389-8900 on the reservations page. dark_sky null: darksky.org page returned 403 and TPWD's dark-sky list does not name this unit.

places.blurb: Ancient flint quarries on the Texas High Plains, seen only on ranger-led tours that must be booked in advance.

places.notes: The NPS planyourvisit page printed no coordinates and gives only a mailing address, P.O. Box 1460, Fritch, TX 79036; no visitor center or HQ address was printed. The point is the GNIS-derived Wikipedia infobox point, so it is not an NPS visitor point. County Potter and acreage 1,371 come from Wikipedia. Camping is null: neither page names a campground, and Wikipedia says only that visits are by reserved ranger-led tour. The 'Hike with a Ranger' link is relative on the NPS page (/alfl/planyourvisit/permitsandreservations.htm); the full URL is my construction from the page's own link. Distances in nearby come from a search summary of NPS and Texas Highways pages, not fetched directly. dark_sky null: darksky.org page returned 403.

places.name: Rio Grande Wild and Scenic River
places.coord_point: rounded point from the Wikipedia infobox (29 deg 29 min N, 103 deg 18 min W); not a visitor center or HQ, approximate only
nearby: Big Bend National Park (administers the river)
places.blurb: Canyon stretches of the Rio Grande, with its upper 69 miles running through Big Bend National Park.
places.status_note: The NPS page links an alerts page whose text I did not read; it says it was last updated August 18, 2023.
places.notes: The NPS page gives only a mailing address: Rio Grande Wild and Scenic River, c/o Big Bend National Park, PO Box 129, Big Bend National Park, TX 79834; phone (432) 477-2251. No street address, HQ name or printed coordinate was found, so the point is Wikipedia's rounded value, which is approximate and should not be used as a visitor point. Counties Brewster, Terrell and Val Verde come from Wikipedia category tags; the point falls in Brewster. Length conflict: NPS says a 196 mile river corridor with the upper 69 miles in Big Bend; Wikipedia gives 260 miles total (Wild 150.1, Scenic 108.5, Recreational 0.8). Wikipedia says Boquillas Canyon is reached through a popular RV campground, but that campground is not named as this unit's camping, so camping is null. nearest_town not stated by either source. dark_sky null: Big Bend National Park carries a dark-sky designation, but it is not confirmed for this river unit, and darksky.org returned 403.
